items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Cause he had Swazee there, he had Randolph, he had Lamar Wright to do it.

ctx.x: Now Billy Butler was gigging around

town, he had a lot of gigs. He would carry me. Renauld Jones was with -- he and I worked with -- Billy Butler would never let me play a solo. He said, no you're a lead trumpet player. Never a solo. One day I played a solo and -- on "Hallelujah" and he said, no, no, no, no. He waved his hands at me and I didn't pay him no mind because I knew what I played was right. But he never wanted me to play a solo. So I think, actually, Cab gave me a few -- quite a lot of solos, but they were nice, pretty things, like "World…

But I played mostly all of his beautiful solos, "Nagasaki," I think he turned me loose a couple of times on that. But he never regarded me as a jazz soloist, but as a lead man I played pretty solos. That's what Cab --
